The Rufous-and-white wren (Thryophilus rufalbus) is a medium-sized neotropical passerine whose life history traits are characteristic of a slow-paced, tropical life-history strategy. Field records indicate that hatchlings emerge from the egg at a wet weight of 1.9 grams [Wwb = 1.9 grams], a modest neonatal mass that aligns closely with the value predicted by allometric relationships within the Troglodytidae.
